correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and first southward ice leg
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening and entire initial southward-to-southeastward leg lie in the generalized Inland Ice setting west of the exposed-rock belt southwest of Kangerlussuaq. The original exposes the opening, first long part and its join to the northeastward return. Surface contours, sub-ice bedrock contours and thickness shading are thematic ice information, not a named river.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastward return through inland ice and nunatak margins
correspondence.finding: All eleven successive parts of the eastward and northeastward return are covered through the mapped ice and scattered exposed-rock outliers. The approach reaches the more densely exposed nunatak margin before the southeastward turn. Every intervening stored join is within the readable original coverage. The map does not identify this succession as a natural river or establish flow between the modeled parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward turn through the ice and exposed-rock corridor
correspondence.finding: The southeastward turn, long descending part and short continuations occupy the generalized ice and exposed-rock corridor west of the Kangerlussuaq coastal area. Both the ice passages and neighboring or intersected bedrock outcrops are distinguished by the original. The full turn and all joins are geographically accounted for, without interpreting crossings of geological or ice symbols as hydraulic connections.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward middle-to-lower ice and rock-margin sequence
correspondence.finding: The eastward succession after the southern turn is fully covered among elongated exposed-rock outcrops and intervening ice. The original includes all short stepped parts, their joins and the transition toward the broader lower-ice setting. No selected lake-throughflow, reservoir, managed channel or continuous named river is established by the cartography.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southeastward steps and eastward leg
correspondence.finding: All lower southeastward steps and the following eastward leg remain within readable mapping of the ice and exposed-rock margin southwest of the Kap Edvard Holm context label. The source accounts for their complete geographic succession and both bounding joins. It supplies generalized historical terrain correspondence, not a precise glacier assignment or present hydraulic behavior.

correspondence.component_scope: Final approach and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The final eastward and southeastward steps, last stored part and actual rendered endpoint are covered within the generalized historical lower-ice and exposed-rock coastal-margin setting southwest of Kap Edvard Holm. The endpoint is in the mapped ice setting between exposed-rock outliers, inland of the generalized outer coast at this source scale. Neither the supplied sea-terminal classification nor nearby coastal place labels establish an ordinary river mouth. Exact modern ice-front position and present land, ice or water assignment are not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northeastern opening
correspondence.finding: The selected opening descends southwest through a headwater segment that is not depicted continuously on either CEHQ original. The mapped upstream line begins farther down the selected corridor. No specific source lake, wetland passage or intervening headwater connection is established, and a nearby blue line is not substituted for the selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward descent into the east–west corridor
correspondence.finding: Below the missing opening, the mapped watercourse follows the selected southwestward descent and bends into the westward corridor. The two regional originals support this connected reach at ordinary corridor scale. Its separate upstream name is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern and central westward corridor
correspondence.finding: The selection follows the mapped westward watercourse through the intermediate joining settings. Nearby northern and southern branches remain distinct; label proximity does not assign Jolicoeur to every tributary. No substantial through-lake or reservoir passage is depicted on this supported section.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern bend and western joining corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected southern bend, return toward the west/northwest and successive connecting reaches are represented by the original watercourse network. Where the regional map depicts closely spaced branches and junctions, the selected continuous corridor remains traceable without demanding bank-level coincidence. No separate scalar name is assigned to an individual branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower confluence setting and northward Jolicoeur
correspondence.finding: The selected western approach enters the mapped northward river corridor in the tributary-confluence setting. Region09 prints Rivière Jolicoeur along this lower river. Region08 and09 distinguish neighboring Rivière à la Truite and Maquet and the eastern Jolicoeur Nord-Est tributary; those labels are not substitutes for the selected corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual coastward ending
correspondence.finding: After the eastern-tributary joining setting, the selection follows the mapped northwestward continuation to Baie James. The source-supported coastal ending belongs to the same lower Jolicoeur corridor. This is ordinary corridor correspondence, not a claim about an exact surveyed mouth, present tidal channels or shoreline position.

correspondence.component_scope: Bull Canyon headward opening and eastward approach to Deep Creek
correspondence.finding: The chosen northern opening follows the Bull Canyon valley setting in the Deep Creek Mountains, then turns east and southeast toward mapped Deep Creek. Readable cartography shows the terrain, roads and nearby drainage but does not establish a continuous selected watercourse across the complete northern opening and eastward transfer. IDFG independently calls Bull Canyon a Deep Creek tributary, supporting the general feeder relationship without supplying the missing selected-route connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Deep Creek, Sheep Creek junction and Holbrook approach
correspondence.finding: The selected southward corridor corresponds to repeatedly labeled Deep Creek along the Arbon Valley setting. The map depicts Sheep Creek joining from the east and carries the Deep Creek corridor to Holbrook. Local model simplification does not prevent ordinary corridor correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Holbrook to Stone Reservoir and downstream continuation
correspondence.finding: Deep Creek continues south from Holbrook into the elongated Stone Reservoir setting and reappears along its mapped downstream channel. Both reservoir approach and exit are visible; separate western drainage and diversion lines are not substituted for the selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: Stone, Idaho–Utah crossing and Snowville
correspondence.finding: The mapped Deep Creek channel and surrounding riparian/wetland corridor continue past Stone, cross the Idaho–Utah boundary and reach Snowville. The selected southward approach and westward turn below the road crossing are covered at corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Rose Ranch Reservoirs and western bend
correspondence.finding: Below Snowville the route bends west through the mapped Rose Ranch Reservoirs setting, then resumes a labeled Deep Creek corridor toward the southwest. Both sides of the impounded setting are depicted. This does not establish current storage, release or irrigation operations.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwest Curlew Valley Deep Creek
correspondence.finding: The selected southwest and southward leg follows a repeatedly labeled Deep Creek channel across Curlew Valley, past the Wildcat Hills/Cedar Hill setting and toward the lower wetland entrance. The source depicts much of this leg with an interrupted blue channel symbol; no perennial-flow claim is made.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Deep Creek, West Lake-side wetlands and selected lakeward transfer
correspondence.finding: The maps carry a Deep Creek label into the broad lower wetland setting west of West Lake. West Lake, East Lake and several sloughs are separately depicted to the east. The selected line then continues south beyond mapped local channels across a broad patterned lake-margin area into the main lake. The sources do not establish that complete selected through-connection. Nearby sloughs and contiguous wetland/lake-margin shading are not treated as proof of the selected transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Great Salt Lake continuation and actual modeled endpoint
correspondence.finding: Beyond the northern lake-margin interval, the selected line continues south and southeast within the mapped Great Salt Lake waterbody to its actual endpoint. All remaining parts and the endpoint were visually inspected. The endpoint is an interior terminal-lake location on this cartography, not an open-sea mouth, a mapped river mouth or proof of an onward Deep Creek channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern opening and initial southwestern descent
correspondence.finding: No original map pixels were available to associate the chosen opening and first southwestern passage with a named watercourse. The municipal hydrography list does not establish which, if any, of its names belongs to these selected parts.

correspondence.component_scope: First westward and northwestern arc with successive joins
correspondence.finding: The selected return to the northwest and subsequent western bends have not been matched to independently inspected mapped channels. Neither a nearby basin name nor the municipal stream list establishes these through-links.

correspondence.component_scope: Central western route, northern bends and intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: No original cartography was inspected for the extended westward interval and its alternating northern bends. The municipality-wide description of dune fields is regional context only and does not prove the selected surface-water connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Western turn and southwestern approach to the long southern course
correspondence.finding: The southwestward turn and its joins into the following southern interval remain uncorresponded. The presence of separately named streams and canals in the municipal table is insufficient to identify a natural or managed passage here.

correspondence.component_scope: Long southern interval, western bend and return toward the southeast
correspondence.finding: The selected long southern course and westernmost bend lack original-map comparison. Any connection across dry ground, irrigation or drainage works, or wetland margins must remain unresolved rather than be inferred from the regional Colorado River and canal names.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern lower course and successive near-terminal joins
correspondence.finding: No source map established the southeastward lower through-links or their relationship to coastal plain and marsh features. No selected lake, wetland, managed connection or naming transition is assumed absent merely because the map was unavailable.

correspondence.component_scope: Final eastward interval and actual modeled coastal ending
correspondence.finding: The model classifies the final endpoint as sea, but no original coastal map was inspected to establish the actual selected river-to-coast connection. The municipal statement that its boundary reaches the Gulf of California cannot supply the missing outlet identity.
